assessment.nobel_worthiness: Introduced a physical-chemical concept of cellular organisation: membraneless compartments as liquid-like condensates formed by phase separation of multivalent proteins and RNA. It brings thermodynamics, phase behaviour and intermolecular interactions into cell biology and has reorganised how compartmentalisation is understood, with wide uptake in neurodegeneration and gene regulation research.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed liquid-like P granule behaviour in 2009; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction framework (signalling-protein phase separation, 2012). Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physical principles for disordered proteins, so the three-person limit forces a difficult choice.
assessment.maturity: Concept widely reproduced, but debate continues on physiological relevance in vivo versus in vitro droplet formation, and on how to separate true phase separation from other assemblies. Timely, though some interpretations are still evolving.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag is contestable.
Extent to which condensates are functionally causal in cells remains debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lipid self-assembly and ionizable-lipid design underpin nanoparticles that deliver nucleic acids, enabling mRNA vaccines and siRNA therapeutics. A molecular-level control of pKa-dependent charge, bilayer-to-non-bilayer phase behaviour and encapsulation is physical chemistry with enormous societal impact.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and Hope (with Madden) developed the early lipid nanoparticle and encapsulation methods; MacLachlan and Cullis advanced ionizable-lipid siRNA formulations; Anderson and Langer contributed lipid libraries and delivery strategies. Credit is spread across academic and industrial groups. I chose the core lipid-assembly contributors, but Anderson or Langer could reasonably be substituted.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at scale, so maturity is very high. Medicine 2023 recognised mRNA modification, which makes a chemistry recognition of the delivery vehicle timely but also raises a question of overlap.
uncertainties: Patent and industrial credit disputes may blur the attribution.
Risk of perceived overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory reduced protein folding to general statistical-mechanical principles, resolving Levinthal's paradox and unifying folding kinetics and thermodynamics. This is the kind of general physical-chemical explanation of a biological phenomenon I value most.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson formulated the funnel landscape; Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model framework; Fersht provided the experimental mapping (phi-value analysis). Attribution is plausible but the theory and experiment halves may need separate treatment.
assessment.maturity: Concept has been established for decades and is broadly accepted; recognition is arguably overdue. AlphaFold's 2024 prize addressed structure prediction rather than folding physics, so this remains open.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should combine theory with Fersht's experiments is unresolved.
Dill versus Fersht versus Bryngelson in the final trio is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers of thiols on gold gave molecular-level control over interfacial structure and wettability, and soft lithography extended this to patterning. A foundational surface and colloid chemistry concept used across biosensing, electronics and cell-surface studies.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported alkanethiol/disulfide monolayers on gold (1983); Whitesides developed the systematic SAM science and soft lithography; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers are a priority matter. Xia's role is mainly soft lithography.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent confirmation and heavy use. Recognition is not premature; competition from newer topics is the main issue.
uncertainties: Priority of Sagiv versus Nuzzo and Allara.
Possible scope mismatch if a prize is meant for SAMs alone versus soft lithography.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase and reveals stoichiometry, interactions and lipid binding of intact protein complexes, including membrane proteins. It links physical chemistry of ions with structural biology and gives chemically detailed views of assemblies.
assessment.attribution: Robinson, Heck and Chait are leading developers of native MS for protein complexes, with Loo and Gross contributing methodological foundations. The 2002 ESI prize covered the underlying ionisation, so the case rests on the application to intact complexes.
assessment.maturity: Technique is widely adopted and independently validated; some caveats concern whether gas-phase structures faithfully reflect solution structures.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier ionisation prize may weigh against it.
Preservation of solution-phase structure in the gas phase is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to degrade targeted proteins changes drug design logic, converting binders into catalytic degraders. It is a conceptual shift in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry with strong clinical momentum.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTACs (2001); Ciulli advanced VHL-based degraders and structural design; Handa, Ito and others uncovered cereblon as the thalidomide target for molecular glues. A fair configuration is complicated because PROTAC and molecular-glue stories have different origins.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still maturing, with many compounds in trials but limited approvals. Possibly slightly premature.
uncertainties: PROTACs and molecular glues are a compound discovery that may require separate recognition.
Clinical efficacy evidence is still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule detection of nucleic acids by passage through a nanopore is a physical-chemical idea turned into a practical sequencing technology, based on ionic current blockades through confined channels.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer demonstrated polynucleotide translocation (1996); Akeson and Deamer advanced the enzyme-based control; Bayley's engineered pores were important. Attribution is plausible but Kasianowicz is also a candidate.
assessment.maturity: Technology widely deployed and validated, with long reads now routine. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Exact weighting between concept (Branton, Deamer) and engineering contributions is uncertain.
I am uncertain about the current status of some credited individuals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites rapidly reached high solar-cell efficiencies, relating defect tolerance and ion-transport physical chemistry to device performance. A major materials-chemistry development, building on the dye-sensitised cell tradition.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cells (2009); Park and Grätzel demonstrated solid-state devices (2012); Snaith made the thin-film breakthrough. Credit is shared among several groups and the sequence is contested.
assessment.maturity: Performance is confirmed, but long-term stability, toxicity and commercial viability are unresolved, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial viability are unresolved.
Attribution among Miyasaka, Park, Grätzel, Snaith and Seok is contested.
